content.user_title: Build Python Job Schedules with APScheduler
content.value_statement: Recurring Python jobs need clear scheduling and persistence choices. This skill guides APScheduler setup for cron, interval, async, and distributed workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains synchronous Scheduler and asynchronous AsyncScheduler setup.
Shows interval, cron, date, and calendar interval trigger patterns.
Demonstrates persistence with SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, SQLite, and event brokers.
Covers FastAPI lifespan integration for background scheduling.
Describes schedule management, job results, and event handling.
Lists package extras for common database and broker backends.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, but does not execute or monitor jobs.
Uses placeholder credentials and URLs that must be replaced safely.
Does not design retry, alerting, or metrics systems by itself.
Requires users to validate APScheduler version compatibility in their project.

use_cases.title: Recurring application maintenance
use_cases.description: Add cleanup, email, report, and cache refresh jobs to Python services.

use_cases.title: Periodic data synchronization
use_cases.description: Schedule async data fetches and database updates at controlled intervals.

use_cases.title: Persistent distributed scheduling
use_cases.description: Plan schedulers and worker roles with shared stores and event brokers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic interval job
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one recurring task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use APScheduler to run my cleanup function every 30 minutes in a Python service.

prompt_templates.title: Add a weekday cron schedule
prompt_templates.scenario: Schedule work at a business time
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to schedule a report job at 9 AM from Monday through Friday with APScheduler.

prompt_templates.title: Persist schedules across restarts
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through using AsyncScheduler with SQLAlchemy persistence so schedules survive restarts.

prompt_templates.title: Design distributed workers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced scaling with scheduler and worker roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an APScheduler setup with separate scheduler and worker nodes using a shared store and event broker.

output_examples.input: I need a job that cleans temporary files every hour.
output: Recommended an interval trigger with a one-hour cadence.
Outlined where to start the scheduler in the application lifecycle.
Flagged the need for error handling in the cleanup function.

output_examples.input: My scheduled jobs disappear after every deployment.
output: Identified in-memory storage as the likely cause.
Recommended a persistent SQLAlchemy data store.
Explained that credentials should come from secure configuration.

output_examples.input: I want one process to create schedules and other processes to run jobs.
output: Suggested separate scheduler and worker roles.
Explained shared data store and event broker requirements.
Listed backend choices that match the documented examples.

best_practices: Use persistent data stores for production schedules that must survive restarts.
Set misfire grace time and coalescing rules for delayed or overlapping runs.
Subscribe to job events so failures are visible to logs or alerts.
anti_patterns: Using memory storage for production jobs that must be durable.
Embedding real credentials in scheduler examples or job arguments.
Scheduling very frequent jobs without concurrency limits or failure handling.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design APScheduler jobs, triggers, persistence, and worker patterns for Python applications.

faq.question: Does it run scheduled jobs for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that you apply inside your own Python project.

faq.question: Can it help with FastAPI applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes the lifespan pattern for starting AsyncScheduler with a FastAPI app.

faq.question: How do jobs survive application restarts?
faq.answer: Use a persistent data store, such as SQLAlchemy with PostgreSQL or SQLite, instead of memory storage.

faq.question: Can APScheduler run distributed workers?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples describe separate scheduler and worker roles with a shared store and event broker.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
